title: Pressure and Proximity Tuned Twisted Bilayer Graphene
authors: David T. S. Perkins, Joseph J. Betouras
abstract: The coupling between layered atomically-thin materials mediated by van der Waals forces allows strong electronic correlations, unique topological signatures, and non-trivial spin textures, all of which play an important role in the creation of spin-, valley-, and orbitronic devices. Here, we demonstrate that twisted bilayer graphene encapsulated by transition metal dichalcogenides exhibits a generically non-radial spin texture yet hosts a purely collinear Edelstein effect despite this lack of radial symmetry. Moreover, we show how uniaxial pressure can be used to further tune the band structure and change the number of active Fermi surfaces without compromising the collinear response. Lastly, we illustrate how the quantum geometry changes in the encapsulated twisted graphene bilayer with larger pressures spreading the Berry curvature over large regions of the moiré Brillouin zone. These results illustrate how encapsulation and pressure can be used to drastically alter the topology and spin-charge interconversion processes of moiré heterostructures.
summary: This work theoretically investigates how encapsulating twisted bilayer graphene with TMDs and applying uniaxial pressure modifies its electronic topology and spin properties. The researchers demonstrate that the system maintains a purely collinear Edelstein effect and that pressure can tune the band structure and redistribute the Berry curvature. These findings highlight the tunability of moiré heterostructures for advanced spintronic applications.
main_problem: To investigate how encapsulation by Transition Metal Dichalcogenides (TMDs) and external uniaxial pressure can drastically alter the topology and spin-charge interconversion processes in moiré heterostructures, specifically twisted bilayer graphene (TBG).
main_result: The system exhibits a purely collinear Edelstein effect even with non-radial spin texture, and uniaxial pressure can tune the band structure, change the number of active Fermi surfaces, and spread the Berry curvature across the moiré Brillouin zone.
method: Theoretical modeling using a continuum Hamiltonian approach, incorporating proximity-induced SOC and pressure effects via interlayer distance modification.
model_or_system: The system is Twisted Bilayer Graphene (TBG) encapsulated by TMDs. The model uses a continuum Hamiltonian derived from the Bistritzer-MacDonald formalism, including terms for SOC and interlayer hopping, with pressure modifying the interlayer distance.
key_observables: Spin texture (collinear Edelstein effect), band structure, Berry curvature distribution, and the number of active Fermi surfaces.
important_parameters: Twist angle ($	heta \approx 1.05^\circ$), applied uniaxial pressure ($P$), and interlayer coupling strengths ($w_0, w_1$).
main_assumptions: The analysis truncates the Hamiltonian to 10 shells for convergence, and the interlayer coupling strength is modeled based on interpolation between AA and AB stacking distances.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the construction of the Moiré Brillouin Zone (MBZ), band structures under varying SOC and pressure, and spin maps showing the evolution of spin texture and Berry curvature.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the effect of encapsulation and pressure on the electronic structure, first establishing the spin texture and Edelstein effect, then detailing how pressure tunes the band topology and the quantum geometry (Berry curvature).
why_interesting: The study explores how external tuning parameters (pressure) can control topological properties and spin-charge coupling in engineered 2D materials, which is highly relevant for designing novel spintronic and valleytronic devices.
